output:
**No, this pipeline is not safe for agent-written infrastructure changes.** It deploys in Complete mode with no preview of what will change, and the deploy identity is subscription Owner. So one approved PR that removes or renames a resource in `infra/main.bicep` deletes it. The orders database and the uploads storage account have no protection against that.

**What I found:** `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` runs `--mode Complete` straight after merge, and `infra/main.bicep` names the database and storage account with editable names and no deletion locks. Block it and add a gate that checks the deploy's effect first (the record calls this BLOCKED / Add gate).

**Why it matters:** One human review of a large agent PR only sees the text. Renaming `storageName` or dropping the `db` block looks harmless there, but it deletes customer data, and redeploying won't bring it back. Without the fix, the first bad agent PR can do this, and Owner rights mean it can also grant itself any role or remove any lock in the subscription.

**Do this first:**
1. In `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:40`, change `--mode Complete` to `--mode Incremental`. Complete mode should be something a single change opts into, never the default.
2. Run `az deployment group what-if` in the PR job and again in the deploy job right before the deploy runs. Fail the job if it would delete or replace the SQL server, the `orders` database, `appproduploads` or `app-prod-kv`.
3. Replace subscription Owner with Contributor on resource group `app-prod` only. Then put `CanNotDelete` locks on the SQL server and storage account; Contributor can't remove them.

**What I did not check:**
- Branch protection, i.e. whether `validate` is a required check and whether agents can approve: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection`
- Whether the `production` environment has required reviewers: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/environments/production`
- The OIDC federated credential subject (if it isn't `environment:production`, the environment gate can be bypassed): `az ad app federated-credential list --id <AZURE_CLIENT_ID>`
- What Complete mode would delete today. The SQL server is declared `existing`, and I'm not sure Complete mode leaves it alone. If it deletes it, the database goes with it: `az deployment group what-if -g app-prod -f infra/main.bicep --mode Complete`
- Existing locks, storage soft-delete/versioning and SQL backup retention: `az lock list -g app-prod`, `az storage account blob-service-properties show -n appproduploads`, `az sql db ltr-policy show`

```
Scope:          .github/workflows/deploy.yml (validate, deploy) → resource group app-prod; infra/main.bicep
Decision:       Block; Add gate; Make idempotent (stop deleting undeclared resources)
Risk:           destructive-change, IaC, preflight, authorization, concurrency, health-check, production-verification
Artifact:       No artifact. The deploy re-reads infra/main.bicep at the push commit; there is no compiled ARM JSON, digest or saved plan tying what was reviewed to what gets applied
Release state:  BLOCKED
Test evidence:  PR runs `az bicep build` and `az bicep lint` only (deploy.yml:21-22). No IaC security scan (PSRule/Checkov), no what-if, no Azure login at PR time, so the reviewer never sees the effect on live resources
Preflight:      None. Deploy runs straight from azure/login to `az deployment group create` (deploy.yml:31-40). No what-if and no deletion/replacement check before the deploy runs
Strategy:       Production-only, with no exposure control. Every merge to main touching infra/** deploys straight to app-prod
Representativeness: n/a (no non-production stage)
Rollout:        In-place ARM deployment in Complete mode (deploy.yml:40). Any resource in app-prod not in the template is deleted. Renaming `storageName` (main.bicep:3) or the `orders` db (main.bicep:11) creates a new empty resource and deletes the old one. No switch, no path back to the previous version
Zero-downtime:  no. Removing or renaming a resource deletes it; a resource that can only be replaced, or a delete-then-create, leaves a gap
Rollback:       None. Redeploying an earlier commit recreates empty resources and doesn't restore orders or uploads
Owner handoff:  missing
Evidence:       deploy.yml:4-8 (pull_request + push triggers), :28 (environment: production; whether it has protection rules is unverified), :36-40 (Complete mode, no what-if), no `concurrency:` block. main.bicep:2-3 (editable names for state-holding resources), :5-7 (SQL server is `existing`), no Microsoft.Authorization/locks. User says the deploy identity is subscription Owner and one human approval is required
Verification:   Not run. No Azure access in this session; what-if, branch protection and environment rules are unverified (listed above)
Next action:    (1) deploy.yml:40 → `--mode Incremental`. (2) Add a what-if step to both jobs that fails on any Delete or Replace for Microsoft.Sql/servers, Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases, Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts or Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults; the PR job needs a read-only (Reader) login. (3) Scope the identity to Contributor on rg app-prod and add CanNotDelete locks outside this template. (4) Add `concurrency: { group: deploy-app-prod, cancel-in-progress: false }`. (5) Require `validate` + what-if as a required check, and add required reviewers on the `production` environment
```

The what-if gate for step 2 can look like this. Put it before line 36 in the deploy job, and add a similar step to `validate` after a Reader-scoped login:

```yaml
      - name: Effect gate (no deletion/replacement of stateful resources)
        run: |
          az deployment group what-if -g app-prod -f infra/main.bicep \
            --mode Incremental --no-pretty-print > whatif.json
          jq -e '[.changes[]
                  | select(.changeType=="Delete" or .changeType=="Replace"
                           or .changeType=="Create")
                  | select(.resourceId | test("Microsoft\\.(Sql/servers|Storage/storageAccounts|KeyVault/vaults)"))]
                 | length == 0' whatif.json
```

`Create` is included so a renamed `storageName`, which shows up as a brand-new empty account beside the old one, is caught too. A release that really is meant to add one of these resources has to name it explicitly in the same PR to get past the gate.
